tokens.name: canvas
tokens.usage: App background behind every screen (Adobe Spectrum's dark background-base). Neutral, untinted gray so the user's colors aren't shifted.

tokens.name: stage
tokens.usage: Behind the video or photo preview inside both editors, as in CapCut, so the frame edges read clearly.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Cards, sheets, bottom navigation, tool bar, timeline lanes (Spectrum layer-1).

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Raised controls on surface: secondary buttons, chips, search field, unselected font tiles, pressed segments, empty media frames. It never marks a selected state (only 1.4:1 against canvas): selection is white.

tokens.name: hairline
tokens.usage: 1px dividers and quiet borders. Decorative only: never the only sign of a control's edge.

tokens.name: text
tokens.usage: Primary text and icons (about 95% white, softer than pure white on near-black). 12.4:1 or more on every surface.

tokens.name: text-secondary
tokens.usage: Supporting text and inactive icons. 5.7:1 or more on canvas, surface and surface-raised.

tokens.name: text-muted
tokens.usage: Hints, placeholders, timecodes and ruler labels. 4.6:1 or more on canvas, surface and surface-raised.

tokens.name: primary
tokens.usage: Memix sky blue: CapCut's cyan moved 9° toward Spectrum blue. The one primary action per screen (Create, Export, Apply), the active tool, links, progress, and everything that is a meme sound. Text on it is on-primary (7.9:1).

tokens.name: primary-pressed
tokens.usage: Pressed state of primary fills. Text on it is on-primary (6.0:1).

tokens.name: primary-subtle
tokens.usage: 16% sky wash behind the active tool, sound play buttons and the "Add a meme sound" pill (over a canvas base). Icons and text on it use primary (6.2:1 over canvas). It never fills a whole row: a playing sound row steps one value up instead (surface on canvas, surface-raised on surface). Pressed, these fills turn surface-raised (primary on it 5.9:1).

tokens.name: on-primary
tokens.usage: Text and icons on primary, primary-pressed, selection-white fills and danger. Also the 1px dark edge beside white selection marks drawn over the user's content (the text frame, its handle and snap guides on the preview, P1-10), so they read on any video: white plus this edge is at least 4.3:1 against any color.

tokens.name: selection
tokens.usage: Selected clip or layer outline, trim handles, playhead, selected chip, segment and font tile fills (text on them on-primary), the selected swatch ring: white, as in CapCut, so selection never competes with clip colors.

tokens.name: track-video
tokens.usage: Main video and overlay clips (they show thumbnails). Labels on it are text.

tokens.name: track-text
tokens.usage: Text clips on the timeline and text layers in the layers panel. Labels on it are on-track (7.5:1).

tokens.name: track-sticker
tokens.usage: Sticker, image and cut-out clips. Labels on it are on-track (9.0:1).

tokens.name: track-meme-sound
tokens.usage: Meme sound clips: the brand color, same as primary, so sound is always Memix blue. Labels on it are on-track (7.9:1).

tokens.name: track-audio
tokens.usage: Original audio, imported audio and voiceover clips: green, the editing convention for audio. Labels on it are on-track (6.8:1).

tokens.name: track-effect
tokens.usage: Effect and filter clips. Labels on it are on-track (6.5:1).

tokens.name: on-track
tokens.usage: Labels and icons on every colored track fill.

tokens.name: danger
tokens.usage: Delete, discard and recording states, always with a word or icon. Text on it is on-primary (5.7:1).

tokens.name: danger-pressed
tokens.usage: Pressed state of danger fills. Text on it is on-primary (4.8:1).

tokens.name: success
tokens.usage: Export finished and saved states, always with a word or icon. Text on it is on-primary (9.3:1).

tokens.name: focus-ring
tokens.usage: Keyboard and switch-access focus: a solid 2px ring, 2px outside the control.

tokens.name: scrim
tokens.usage: Behind bottom sheets and dialogs. On the timeline: the wash over the part of an item past the end of the video (its label switches to text), and the selected main clip's duration badge (text on it is 7.5:1 or more over any thumbnail).

fonts.note: Hindi display face (P1-17) and the Devanagari partner of Anton in captions (P1-10). Alternative: the variable https://github.com/google/fonts/blob/main/ofl/teko/Teko%5Bwght%5D.ttf (285 KB, weights 300 to 700), only if Compose Multiplatform resources can set its weight axis on Android and iOS.
Caption font 'Modern' (P1-10). Indian Type Foundry; Latin, Latin Ext, Devanagari.
Caption font 'Bubbly' (P1-10). Ek Type; Latin, Latin Ext, Vietnamese, Devanagari. Static build from the upstream that google/fonts names (its own file is the 667 KB variable Baloo2[wght].ttf).
Caption font 'Handwritten' (P1-10). Indian Type Foundry; Latin, Latin Ext, Devanagari.
Caption font 'Serif' (P1-10). Indian Type Foundry; Latin, Latin Ext, Devanagari.

groups.name: Display
groups.note: Anton, Google Fonts (SIL OFL). Meme captions, the wordmark and the Home hero only.

styles.name: display-xl
styles.usage: Home hero and empty-state headlines, uppercase.

styles.name: display
styles.usage: Entry cards and sheet heroes, uppercase.

styles.name: wordmark
styles.usage: The Memix name (Home top bar, until a logo exists). Always Anton, in every language: unlike display, it never switches to the Hindi face. Written as is, not uppercased.

styles.name: meme-caption
styles.usage: Default caption style in both editors: white fill with a 3px black outline stroke (the classic meme look; this is the user's content, not chrome).

groups.name: Display (Hindi)
groups.note: Teko Bold, Indian Type Foundry (SIL OFL 1.1): Latin, Latin Extended and Devanagari. Replaces the Display group's display-xl and display when the app language is Hindi (P1-17), for the whole string, Latin letters included. The Memix wordmark stays Anton. Letter spacing 0, because tracking breaks the Devanagari headline bar.

styles.name: display-xl
styles.usage: Hindi: Home hero and empty-state headlines. The line height is Teko's own line spacing (1.433 em; the candrabindu and the vocalic-rr sign reach its full ascent and descent), rounded up to the 4px grid, so no mark above the headline bar or below the baseline is cut (P1-17 build, 9 Oct 2026).

styles.name: display
styles.usage: Hindi: entry cards and sheet heroes. Line height from Teko's own line spacing, as display-xl.

groups.name: Caption sample
groups.note: Set in the caption font it previews (caption.fonts), at that file's own weight. The only interface text not in Space Grotesk, Space Mono or the display faces, because the sample is the choice.

styles.name: caption-sample
styles.usage: The name on each FontTile in the Style panel (P1-10), drawn in that font. Line height 28 leaves room for Devanagari marks above and below in every caption font.

groups.name: Interface
groups.note: Space Grotesk, Google Fonts (SIL OFL). Sentence case everywhere.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Pick a clip, drop a sound, share it.

styles.name: caption
styles.usage: Tool bar labels, metadata, timeline clip labels.

styles.name: timecode
styles.usage: Playback timecode, ruler marks, durations in the editors.

spacing.note: 4px base. Screen side gutter is space-4.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Icon-to-label gap, gaps between clips on a track.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Inside chips and small controls.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Between related rows and chips.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Screen side gutter, card and sheet padding.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Button side padding, tab gaps.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Between sections.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Above screen titles, large section breaks.

tokens.name: space-10
tokens.usage: Empty-state padding.

radius.note: Chunky, never sharp; pills for chips and tabs.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Timeline clips, badges.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Buttons, inputs, the Create button, tool highlights.

tokens.name: radius-lg
tokens.usage: Cards, sheets, template thumbnails.

tokens.name: radius-full
tokens.usage: Chips, segmented tabs, play buttons.

shadow.note: No hard or decorative shadows: surfaces separate by value steps (canvas → surface → surface-raised), as in CapCut and Spectrum. Only sheets and floating menus cast a soft shadow.

tokens.name: shadow-sheet
tokens.usage: Bottom sheets lifting over a screen.

tokens.name: shadow-float
tokens.usage: Floating menus and toasts.

tokens.name: stroke-hairline
tokens.usage: Dividers and quiet borders, with the hairline color.

tokens.name: stroke-selection
tokens.usage: Selected clip or layer outline, with the selection color.

tokens.name: stroke-focus
tokens.usage: Focus ring width, offset 2px.

size.note: Fixed sizes used across screens (dp on Android).

tokens.name: touch-target
tokens.usage: Minimum tappable size for every control.

tokens.name: nav-height
tokens.usage: Bottom navigation bar.

tokens.name: toolbar-height
tokens.usage: Editor tool bar.

tokens.name: tool-item-width
tokens.usage: Minimum width of one tool in the editors' tool bars (icon over a caption label, at least touch-target tall). A tool widens only when one word of its label can't fit at large font sizes. About five and a half tools show at 360 wide, so the first tools never need a scroll (P1-06).

tokens.name: track-height-video
tokens.usage: Main video track clips.

tokens.name: track-height
tokens.usage: Every other track's clips.

tokens.name: playhead-width
tokens.usage: Timeline playhead line, in selection white.

tokens.name: playhead-head-size
tokens.usage: Diameter of the round head on top of the timeline playhead, in selection white, centered on the line at the top of the ruler.

tokens.name: trim-handle-width
tokens.usage: Width of the white trim handles at both ends of the selected timeline item, just outside its selection outline. The touch target around each handle is still touch-target wide.

tokens.name: icon-small
tokens.usage: Icons inside timeline items and badges, where a 24px icon doesn't fit (for example the lock on a locked item). The same drawings as the 24px set, scaled down; never for standalone controls.

tokens.name: rail-height
tokens.usage: The thin rail under a fill: progress bar and slider. Rail in hairline, fill in primary. Called rail, not track, because a track is a timeline lane in Memix.

tokens.name: canvas-handle-size
tokens.usage: Diameter of the white scale-and-rotate handle on a selected text (later stickers and layers) on the preview, with a 1px on-primary edge and an icon-small icon in on-primary. Its touch target is still touch-target (P1-10).

tokens.name: swatch-size
tokens.usage: Diameter of a color swatch (text and outline colors, later brush colors). Drawn inside a touch-target square; the selected ring sits 2px outside it (P1-10).

tokens.name: list-thumb-size
tokens.usage: Square thumbnail at the start of a list row (a draft's first frame, P1-14), radius-sm, with the type badge in its corner. The row is at least this plus space-2 above and below.

tokens.name: badge-size
tokens.usage: Side of a square icon badge drawn over the user's picture (the type badge on a draft's thumbnail, P1-14): a scrim chip in radius-sm with an icon-small icon centered, so the 16px icon has 2px around it (its drawing already keeps 1.3px of air inside the 16px box). Placed space-1 from the picture's corner. Not for text badges, which size to their text.

tokens.name: play-disc-size
tokens.usage: Diameter of the big play button centered on a video that isn't playing (the Exported screen, P1-12): a radius-full disc in primary with a 24px play icon in on-primary (7.9:1). It only draws; the tap belongs to the whole video, so the target is far above touch-target. Not for icon controls: those are IconButtons.

tokens.name: icon-medium
tokens.usage: Icons drawn inside a 36 to 40px control or field, where 24px crowds it: the search field's magnifier, the play and pause glyph in a sound's play disc, the create glyph in its Use block (P3-02). The same drawings as the 24px set, scaled; never for a standalone control (those are IconButtons at 24px).

tokens.name: radio-dot-size
tokens.usage: Diameter of the dot inside a selected radio mark (P3-10 Report reasons): an `on-primary` disc centered in a `selection` disc of `icon-medium` (20px), 40% of it. Unselected: a `stroke-selection` ring in `text-secondary`, no dot. The mark sits in a row of at least `touch-target`; the row takes the tap.

tokens.name: sound-disc-size
tokens.usage: Visible diameter of a sound's play disc (SoundRow, P1-08) and of the static placeholder disc on the Sounds screen's loading rows (P3-02). The disc sits in a touch-target square, so the tap area stays 48px. Not for thumbnails (layer-thumb-size) or the big play button (play-disc-size).

tokens.name: layer-thumb-size
tokens.usage: Square thumbnail at the start of a LayerRow in the photo editor's Layers panel (P2-01), radius-sm, showing the layer's picture fitted inside (no checkerboard). The row is at least this plus space-2 above and below, 56px. Smaller than list-thumb-size (the Drafts row's 56px) because ten rows share a panel capped at 40% of the window.

tokens.name: filter-tile-size
tokens.usage: Side of a filter tile's square picture in the Edit photo panel's Filters strip (P2-04): radius-md, the user's photo with that filter on, the name in caption text under it. At least touch-target each way; the thumbnail is made at about 3x this size. Not for other tiles (OptionTile sizes itself).

tokens.name: pack-row-height
tokens.usage: Minimum height of a row on the WhatsApp Packs screen (P2-09): tray 48px, name and count; grows with text at large font.

tokens.name: emoji-row-height
tokens.usage: Minimum height of a sticker row in the Emojis sheet's list pane (P2-09): thumbnail 48px, its emojis, a chevron.

tokens.name: pack-tray-size
tokens.usage: Side of the pack's tray picture on the Added screen (P2-09), on surface-raised, radius-lg.

tokens.name: grid-tile-min
tokens.usage: Minimum width of a sticker tile in the sticker grids (Stickers sheet P2-14 and the pack builder P2-09): the grid takes as many equal columns as fit (3 at 360 dp), each at least this wide. Never below touch-target.

tokens.name: nav-row-height
tokens.usage: Height of a one-tap navigation row inside a sheet (the Stickers sheet's WhatsApp packs row, P2-09): surface-raised, radius-md, icon 24px, title and subtitle, chevron.

tokens.name: sheet-max-height-fraction
tokens.usage: Unitless share of the window height a content sheet (Stickers, Emojis) may use before its content scrolls (P2-14, P2-09).

tokens.name: pinned-bar-max-fraction
tokens.usage: Unitless share of the window height the pinned bottom area of the pack builder (counter and buttons) may take at large font before the counter scrolls with the content and only the buttons stay pinned (P2-09). Also the sound picker sheet's pinned header, search plus tabs (P3-05): past this share the search field scrolls with the list and only the title and tabs stay pinned. Also the Audio effects panel's pinned part, title row plus tabs (P3-09): past this share of the panel the tabs scroll with the content and only the title row stays.

tokens.name: waveform-bar-width
tokens.usage: Width of one waveform bar (P3-03): radius-full ends. Bars are resampled from the sound's peaks to fill the width, one bar per bar-width plus waveform-bar-gap.

tokens.name: waveform-bar-gap
tokens.usage: Gap between waveform bars (P3-03).

tokens.name: waveform-height
tokens.usage: Height of a waveform inside a SoundRow (P3-03), centered on its midline. A bar is never shorter than waveform-bar-width, so silence still draws a line. Played bars primary, the rest text-muted (4.6:1 or more on canvas, surface and surface-raised).

tokens.name: waveform-height-large
tokens.usage: Height of the waveform in the sound details sheet (P3-03). Same bars and colors; not a scrub control.

tokens.name: waveform-clip-opacity
tokens.usage: Unitless opacity of the `on-track` bars drawn inside a meme sound or audio clip on the timeline (P3-09). Same bar width and gap as the rows; bar height follows the clip's volume and fades. About 3.3:1 on `track-audio` and 3.6:1 on `track-meme-sound` (SC 1.4.11 needs 3:1); the clip's label sits on a solid patch of the clip color so no bar runs behind a letter.

tokens.name: keyframe-marker-size
tokens.usage: Side of a keyframe diamond (a square turned 45 degrees) on the timeline's marker row and as the badge on a keyed clip (P4-02b): text-secondary on surface-raised 5.7:1 in the row; text with a 1px on-primary edge as the badge over thumbnails (4.3:1 or more over any picture). The diamond's target is touch-target wide in a track-height + space-1 row (the documented non-video exception).

tokens.name: keyframe-marker-size-selected
tokens.usage: Side of the selected keyframe's diamond on the marker row (P4-02b): selection white on surface-raised 14:1. A keyframe at the playhead is selected. Size also changes, so selection is never color alone.

tokens.name: beat-marker-size
tokens.usage: Width of a beat marker's solid downward triangle on the timeline ruler (P4-14; height 6px): text-secondary on canvas 5.7:1. Its target is touch-target wide on the ruler row (the documented non-video exception; Previous, Next and the playhead actions are the equal routes).

tokens.name: beat-marker-size-selected
tokens.usage: Width of the selected beat marker's triangle (P4-14; height 9px): selection white on canvas 17.2:1. The size also changes, so selection is never color alone.

tokens.name: duration-press
tokens.usage: Presses, toggles, nav item color changes, and the reduce-motion fade that replaces every movement.

tokens.name: duration-sheet
tokens.usage: Bottom sheets sliding in and out, tab content changes.

tokens.name: duration-screen
tokens.usage: Screen pushes and pops.

tokens.name: duration-bonk
tokens.usage: The bonk: content landing on the timeline scales 1 to 1.12 to 1 with a slight overshoot. The width grows by the same dp as the height (or 12% if that's less), so a long clip doesn't sweep over its neighbors. Only for placing content.

caption.note: User content, not chrome: how captions (TextItem, TextLayer) render in both editors and in export. Never read through MemixTheme; the engineer keeps these in one commonMain place shared by the engines and both editors. Values are part of every saved draft's look: changing one after P1 ships needs a schema bump and a compensating migration. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P1-10-text.md.

fonts.name: Classic
fonts.usage: The Impact meme look and the default. Devanagari characters are drawn in Teko Bold (whole clusters, never split); emoji and other scripts in the system font.

defaults.usage: A new text uses the last style picked in the current editor visit, otherwise these.

geometry.devanagariSizeFactorNote: Provisional. Size of Teko Bold's Devanagari runs inside a Classic (Anton) caption, relative to the caption's font size. Set at phase-end QA, before the Phase 1 gate, from the mixed-line screenshot: Anton cap height / Teko headline height, rounded to 0.05, or 1.0 if within 5% (P1-10 review).
geometry.usage: Laid out once in canvas pixels, then drawn scaled. Outline stroke = font size / 12, centered on the outline, drawn before the fill.

shadow.usage: P2-11. The silhouette of the text with its outline, in the chosen palette color at 60%, offset down and right in the caption's own space (it turns with the caption), blurred by the softness step. Drawn after the box and before the outline and fill. Never part of the selection frame or the hit area. em = the caption's font size (8% of the shorter side at scale 1, times the layer's scale). Fixed rules: changing one after the closed test needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-11-text-shadow-and-box.md.

box.usage: P2-11. One opaque rectangle around the whole laid-out block (not per line), padded 0.30 em at the sides and 0.18 em above and below, in the chosen palette color, drawn first. The selection frame, the hit area, the measurer and the ratio-change rule use the box. Hidden for bubble words (the bubble body is the box). Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-11-text-shadow-and-box.md.

canvas.note: User content, not chrome: the video canvas's shape and what fills it, drawn alike in preview and export (P1-11). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place next to the caption constants. Values are part of every saved draft's look: changing one after P1 ships needs a schema bump and a compensating migration. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P1-11-canvas.md.

custom.usage: w:h reduced to lowest terms; size = w*k by h*k, where k is the even whole number nearest 1080 / min(w, h). Both sides even, the ratio exact. The long side may be at most 2.39 times the short side (X's accepted range).

defaults.usage: Every new video project (P1-01). Black bars are the meme look: the first caption slot lands on the bar above a landscape clip.

image.usage: P2-12, both editors: a picture the user picks from the gallery fills the canvas (cover, centered crop, no pan or zoom) at the bottom of the stack: behind Fit clips in the video editor, behind every layer in the photo editor. Full brightness, no blur or dimming. A picture whose file is missing draws black. Remove goes back to the editor's default color. Gaps and missing clips stay black, as for the colors and Blur. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-12-canvas-background-image.md.

background.usage: Color: fills the canvas behind fitted clips. Blur: a Fill-scaled copy of the playing clip, Gaussian sigma = 3% of the output's shorter side (32 px at 1080p), full brightness. Gaps and missing clips are always black.

layers.usage: On a ratio change, a layer that was fully inside the frame and now crosses an edge moves in until it is this margin inside; one too big shrinks first (not below caption.geometry.scaleMin). A layer that was partly outside keeps its center and size.

photo.note: User content, not chrome: how the photo editor's canvas and layers start, behave and draw, alike in the editor and in export (P2-01, P2-13). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a PhotoCatalog) next to CaptionCatalog and CanvasCatalog. Values are part of every saved draft's look: changing one after P2 ships needs a schema bump and a compensating migration. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-01-photo-editor-shell.md.

defaults.usage: A blank canvas (the Create sheet's blank row, shown from P2-03), and the background of every photo start. White shows the frame against the black stage, and square posts everywhere without a crop. A photo start takes the photo's own shape instead (photoShape).

photoShape.usage: The canvas of a picked photo: the photo's width / height as shown (EXIF turn applied); a preset ratio if within 1%; otherwise the custom ratio with the fewest terms (1 to 99 each) within 1% of it. A photo more extreme than 2.39:1 either way gets 31:13 or 13:31 and sits whole inside it. Canvas size follows canvas.ratios and canvas.custom (shorter side about 1080 px).

image.sizeAtScale1: fitted inside the canvas, centered; recomputed from the canvas shape at draw time
image.usage: An image layer at scale 1 is the picture scaled to the largest size that lies wholly inside the canvas. A picture within 1% of the canvas's shape covers it instead, so no sliver of background shows. Scale runs 10% to 500% of that size (text keeps caption.geometry.scaleMin and scaleMax: 25% to 500%).

layers.usage: Opacity 10% to 100%, default 100% (a layer at 0% would be invisible but selectable; Hide exists for that). A duplicate sits 3% of the shorter side right and down of its original. On a ratio change a layer that was fully inside moves in just far enough to touch the edge (margin 0 for images, 2% for text and stickers, shrinking first if too big); a layer placed partly outside keeps its center and scale. Images are decoded at the size they are drawn, never above their source or 4096 px on the long side. See canvas.layers for the video rule.

sticker.sizeAtScale1: longer side = 35% of the canvas's shorter side, shape kept, centered; recomputed from the canvas at draw time
sticker.usage: P2-03. A sticker layer is a picture with transparency, drawn small on the meme: at scale 1 its longer side is 35% of the canvas's shorter side (378 px on a 1080 canvas), not fitted inside the frame like a photo layer. No cover rule. Scale 10% to 500% of that size (3.5% to 175% of the shorter side). Fixed rules: changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. P2-14 (picker) and P4-12 (video stickers) use the same rule. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-03-photo-text-and-stickers.md.

text.usage: P2-03. A new text layer lands centered, scale 100%, at the first free slot of top (0.25), bottom (0.75), middle (0.5); a slot is taken when a visible text layer's center is within 0.1 of it; all taken: the middle. It lands at the front of the stack and is selected. The caption look is caption.* (unchanged); a text keeps scale 25% to 500% (caption.geometry). On a ratio change a text fully inside moves in to the 2% margin, shrinking first (not below 25%) if too big. Opacity draws the whole caption as one group (no outline show-through).

cutout.note: P2-07. User content, not chrome: how a background cut-out is stored and drawn (non-destructive: a mask file, refine strokes and a softness on the image layer). Fixed rules; changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-07-background-removal.md.
cutout.maskFormat: 8-bit alpha, WebP lossless or PNG, in the picture's own coordinate space
cutout.pipelinePosition: step 1 with the picture; later steps keep the alpha
cutout.usage: All detected subjects are kept; Erase and Restore strokes are vectors; the cut-out never rewrites the photo; Save as sticker writes the cut-out (without the layer's crop and color edits) to the on-device sticker store.

draw.note: P2-05. User content, not chrome. Fixed rules: changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-05-draw-and-censor.md.
draw.caps: round caps and joins, opaque color, no pressure
draw.pointsUnit: units of the canvas's shorter side, relative to the layer's own center
draw.hitArea: the strokes' bounding box plus half the widest stroke, grown to touch-target; never the whole canvas
draw.usage: A Draw session makes one drawing layer; the eraser is a stroke in the same layer that clears inside the layer's own group; drawing again with the layer selected adds to it.

censor.note: P2-05. User content, not chrome. The minimums are what make a censor safe: part of every draft's look, so a change after the closed test needs a schema bump. a = the area's shorter side, S = the canvas's shorter side.

pixelate.gridAnchor: canvas top-left, in units of S, not turned with the area
pixelate.reviewNote: P2-05b review: was 1/8 to 1/3; a box snug around a line of text left 8 blocks across the text, which can be read. 1/5 is at most 5 blocks across the area.

blur.reviewNote: P2-05b review: was 0.12 to 0.35 of a with a 0.012 S floor; text filling a snug box stayed legible at strength 0 (sigma about a fifth of the text height). A snug box needs sigma of about a quarter of its side.

censor.usage: A backdrop effect: blurs or pixelates what is drawn under it inside its shape, never what is above. Strength 0 is the minimum, never off. No opacity control; the model keeps opacity at 1.

imageTools.note: P2-04. User content, not chrome: how crop, rotate, flip, straighten, adjustments, the 20 filters and deep-fry look on an image layer, alike in the editor, the render hook and export (and the ids and LUT data P4-07 reuses for video). Parameters on the layer, never a new file. Fixed rules: changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-04-image-tools.md.
imageTools.colorSpace: sRGB gamma, 8-bit, clamped after each step

sharpen.formula: unsharp mask, radius 0.0015 of the shorter side, amount a * 1.5

filters.source: original recipes, generated by a script (owner, 2 Nov by delegation): no third-party pack; script and README in the repo
filters.usage: out = mix(color, lut(color), intensity). Ids are saved forever and never renamed.

deepFry.usage: One recipe scaled by the amount; the grain value is a fixed hash of its cell's coordinates so every output size draws the same grain.

geometry.usage: The crop is stored as fractions of the rotated, flipped and straightened picture. The cropped picture is fitted inside the canvas as any image layer; a crop never changes the canvas.

export.note: P2-08. How a photo leaves the editor. Behavior constants, not chrome; never read through MemixTheme. Remembered between exports in multiplatform-settings (app-wide, separate from video's), never in a draft. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-08-photo-export.md.

sizes.usage: The canvas's shorter side in pixels (1x and 2x of the canvas size); the long side follows the canvas shape. Photo exports never scale below the canvas size.

estimateMbPerMegapixel.note: Assumption, replaced by measured values per format after the first exports on the phone (log estimate and actual).

export.alpha: The canvas is opaque; any transparent pixel is flattened onto the canvas background in JPG and kept as drawn in PNG.
export.watermark: Same rules as video (watermark block), drawn last, 4% of S, 3% margins. Applies to Save and Copy; never to sticker files or WhatsApp packs.

workTargetsSeconds.usage: Assumption, measured on the owner's phone at QA.

stickerPack.note: P2-09. WhatsApp sticker packs. Limits come from WhatsApp's official Android README (read 5 Nov 2026; the engineer re-verifies at the start of the build). Behavior constants, never read through MemixTheme. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-09-whatsapp-sticker-pack.md.

stickers.usage: Static only in v1. Each sticker is fitted inside 512 x 512 on a transparent background; quality is searched down until the file is 100 KB or less. Pack order = My stickers order, newest first.

name.usage: WhatsApp allows 128; the screen caps it at 30 so it fits WhatsApp's list.

stickerPack.identifier: A UUID made once per pack and never changed (letters, digits, - and _ only). image_data_version is bumped on every change to the pack's stickers, emojis, name or tray.

formats.note: P2-02. Every size is in S, the canvas's shorter side (1080 px at 1x export, 2160 px at 2x), so a format scales exactly with the export size. Formats draw inside the canvas and never change its ratio or size. Draw order: background, format parts, layers. Fixed rules: changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P2-02-meme-formats.md.
formats.defaultNote: A new photo project and every draft saved before P2-02 have no format (plain). Classic is an explicit choice (owner, 28 Oct).

classic.style: last style used this visit, else caption.defaultStyle

captionBar.usage: A white bar across the top, full width, drawn under the layers. The picture area is the canvas below it. The bar slot ignores the last-style rule (white text on the white bar would vanish).

demotivational.usage: The whole canvas is painted black; a white frame is drawn inset 0.10 S on the left, right and top and ending 0.40 S above the bottom; the picture area is inside it, inset 0.02 S more. The poster hides the canvas background color or image.

panels.usage: 2 to 6 cells edge to edge except a gutter (and the same margin around), showing the canvas background. Cover-fitted photos, zoom 100% to 500%, always covering the cell. An empty cell draws the background in the render and the export. Layers draw above the cells. Grid = 3: one wide on top and two below; 4: 2x2; 5: two on top and three below; 6: two rows of three.

bubbles.usage: A bubble is a layer: the body grows around its words (60% of the caption size, wrapped at 55% of S, padding 0.45 em by 0.35 em); body and tail are one filled shape with one round-joined stroke. The tail tip is stored as an offset from the body's center in body widths and heights and stays within 2 of them. Speech: rounded rectangle; Round: ellipse; Thought: ellipse with a trail of three circles.

stage.usage: The photo editor's canvas frame is inset space-4 on the stage (the video editor uses space-2) so a full-bleed layer's handle lies whole on the stage. A panel is as tall as its content up to 40% of the window height, and the stage refits above it (200 ms scale).

overlay.note: User content, not chrome: how a picture-in-picture overlay (a video or photo clip on an overlay lane of the video editor) lands, is sized, stacked, faded and moved, alike in preview and export (P4-01). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (an OverlayCatalog) next to CanvasCatalog and PhotoCatalog. Values are part of every saved draft's look: changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-01b-overlay-layers.md.

landing.usage: A new overlay starts at the playhead, 3 s for a photo, its own length for a video, cut to end at the end of the video; with under 1 s left it lands ending at the end, as the smaller of its length and 3 s. It lands at 50% of the size fitted inside the canvas, in the first free slot of center, lower right, upper right, lower left, upper left (a slot is taken when a visible overlay's center is within 0.1 of it; all taken: the center), rotation 0, opacity 100%. It lands on the first lane free for its whole span that lies below every lane holding an overlapping item, else a new lane under the last overlay lane.

size.sizeAtScale1: the picture, with its crop and turn, fitted inside the canvas, centered; recomputed from the canvas shape at draw time
size.usage: The photo layers' rule (photo.image): scale 10% to 500% of the fitted size; a picture within 1% of the canvas's shape covers it.

opacity.usage: Per clip; the whole overlay is multiplied once. 10% minimum, because a 0% overlay can't be hit on the stage; keyframes (P4-02) may fade to 0.

gestures.usage: The caption gestures (P1-10) with one addition: the overlay's sides snap flush to the canvas edges. One SegmentTick per engagement.

overlay.stacking: The order of the OVERLAY tracks in the timeline is the paint order, first = back; main video first, then overlays, then text, stickers and effects. A lane lower in the editor's list is in front.
overlay.usage: A duplicate starts where its original ends, so it keeps the same place and is never offset. On a ratio change an overlay fully inside stays fully inside (margin 0, shrunk first if too big, not below 10%); one placed partly outside keeps its center and scale.

clipFrame.note: User content, not chrome: how a video clip's crop, quarter turns, mirrors, Fit or Fill and framing (move, size, turn on the preview) draw, alike in preview and export (P4-16). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place next to OverlayCatalog. Parameters on the clip, never a new file. Fixed rules: changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-16-clip-crop-rotate-flip-fit.md.
clipFrame.pipelineNote: Extended in P4-04: key (P4-04) and color edits (P4-07) follow the crop; the mask (P4-03b) sits in the clip's own box before framing so it moves with the clip; blend (P4-03a) is last, over everything beneath.

geometry.cropFrameSource: the clip's frame at the playhead if inside the clip, else its first frame
geometry.usage: The meaning and order of P2-04's geometry (photo.imageTools.geometry) without Straighten. A cropped clip's shape is the crop's; Fit and Fill apply to it.

framing.sizeAtScale1: the clip's own Fit or Fill size (main clips), fitted inside the canvas (overlays)
framing.usage: Main clips only (overlays use overlay.*). The selected main clip can be dragged, pinched and twisted, or moved with the Position panel; Reset puts it back.

clipFrame.blurBackgroundCopy: the clip with its crop, turns and mirrors, without its framing
clipFrame.usage: Tapping Fit or Fill on a clip (or the Canvas panel's Fit or Fill on every clip) puts the framing back to the default in the same step. Replace clears the crop, turns and mirrors and keeps Fit or Fill and the framing. A clip whose shape is within 1% of the canvas's makes Fit and Fill alike.

chromaKey.note: User content, not chrome: how green screen keying draws on a main clip or an overlay, alike in preview and export (P4-04). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a ChromaKeyCatalog) next to OverlayCatalog. Starting values: the reference renders in docs/qa/references/P4-04-green-screen/ pin them. Changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-04-green-screen.md.

formula.colorSpace: YCbCr BT.601 full range; only Cb and Cr are compared, luma is ignored
formula.distance: distance between the pixel's (Cb, Cr) and the key's, each in -0.5 to 0.5
formula.maxReachNote: Cap on t + f: feather = min(featherBase + featherSoftnessGain x softness, max(featherBase, maxReach - tolerance)), so white (0.328 from the green key) stays fully opaque at every slider setting.
formula.bleedGuardNote: Below this alpha the pixel's chroma along the key's direction is neutralized fully (rising to spillReduction at it), so green never bleeds into a scaled edge. Engine detail, only touches nearly invisible pixels.
formula.rangeNote: Reviewed in P4-04: tolerance 0.05 to 0.25 and feather 0.02 to 0.10 keep a white shirt (distance 0.33 from the green) and skin whole at either slider's 100%.
formula.alpha: smoothstep(tolerance, tolerance + feather, distance), multiplied into the clip's own alpha
formula.spillNote: Where alpha is above 0 the pixel's chroma along the key's direction is reduced by 60% x (1 - alpha) toward neutral. Fixed, no control.

chromaKey.pipelinePosition: after crop, before color edits and Fit or Fill
chromaKey.usage: Opening the Green screen panel on an unkeyed item turns keying on at the defaults (Green, strength 50%, edge softness 25%) as one undo step. Strength moves the tolerance, edge softness the feather. The eyedropper samples the average of 9 x 9 source pixels under the finger from the clip's own picture. Replace keeps the key; Split and Duplicate copy it.

keyframes.note: User content, not chrome: how keyframes are made, stored and evaluated, alike in preview and export (P4-02). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a KeyframeCatalog) next to OverlayCatalog. Fixed rules: changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-02b-keyframes.md.

caption: position
scale
rotation
sticker: opacity if the sticker has it

easings.hold: the left keyframe's look until the next keyframe's time, then a jump

interpolation.rotation: linear in the stored angle, never wrapped

keyframes.usage: A keyframe holds the whole look of an item at a time (position, scale, rotation, opacity and volume where the item has them) with the easing of the segment after it. Once an item has keyframes every edit of it writes one; the first edit in the keyframe bar also writes a keyframe at the item's start holding the old look. Trim keeps keyframes outside the new range in the project, hidden. Split adds an interpolated keyframe at the cut on both pieces.

blendMask.note: User content, not chrome: blend modes for overlays and shape masks for clips, alike in preview and export (P4-03). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a BlendMaskCatalog) next to OverlayCatalog. Ids are saved forever. Starting values: the reference renders in docs/qa/references/P4-03-blend-masks/ pin them. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-03b-shape-masks-and-blend.md.
blendMask.blendSpace: sRGB gamma space on 8-bit values, the W3C separable blend modes and compositing formula; opacity applies first, then the blend over everything beneath

mask.space: the clip's own box after turn, mirror, crop and Fit or Fill, before framing; fractions of that box

blendMask.usage: Ten blend modes plus Normal as a tile row; four mask shapes plus None as tiles, with edge softness, invert, rounded corners (rectangle only) and a Position tab (Width, Height, Rotation, Move, Center) as the single-pointer route. The mask frame shows only while the Mask panel is open.

videoLook.note: User content, not chrome: the video editor's Filters tool (P4-07, an addendum to P2-04). It reuses photo.imageTools for every filter id, LUT, formula and adjustment, so the data lives once. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-07-video-filters-addendum.md.

scope.mainBar: every main clip, one undo step
scope.clipBar: that clip only (main clip or overlay)
scope.newClips: take the look every main clip shares, none when mixed

videoLook.pipelinePosition: after key, before Fit or Fill: brightness, contrast, saturation, warmth, filter, sharpen, vignette
videoLook.vignetteAndSharpenMeasuredOn: the clip's own cropped picture, not the canvas
videoLook.usage: A look on the whole video is two taps (Filters, a tile). Thumbnails show geometry only. A mixed look shows no selected tile; a change writes that one setting to every main clip.

effects.note: User content, not chrome: video effects as items on the Effects lane (P4-06). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (an EffectCatalog) next to OverlayCatalog. Ids are saved forever. Starting values: the reference renders in docs/qa/references/P4-06-effects/ pin them. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-06-video-effects.md.

envelopes.steady: ramps in and out over min(80 ms, length / 4)
envelopes.punch: 0 to full over 80 ms Bezier (0, 0, 0.58, 1); holds to 70% of the length; back to 0 by the end Bezier (0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)
envelopes.decay: full at the start, then exp(-4 t / length)
envelopes.ramp: 0 to full by the end Bezier (0.42, 0, 0.58, 1), then a jump back at the item's end

effects.scope: the whole composed frame (main video, overlays, captions, stickers), never the watermark; after the clip pipeline
effects.stackingOrder: lane order, first lane applied first
effects.randomness: a hash of the frame time rounded to 1/30 s and a per-effect constant, never a live random number

photosensitivity.note: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.1; Flash is one burst per item, Light pulse 2 Hz, Glitch at most 3 bursts a second

effects.usage: An effect is an item on the Effects lane placed at the playhead from the Effects sheet (three-column grid of the user's frame with the effect, tabs per group); it keeps its length and intensity when replaced. Parameters are shares of the output's shorter side so the preview and the export match.

transitions.note: User content, not chrome: transitions between main-track clips (P4-08). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a TransitionCatalog) next to OverlayCatalog. Ids are saved forever. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-08-transitions.md.
transitions.window: centered on the cut: [cut - d/2, cut + d/2]
transitions.audio: never touched: the project's audio is identical with the transition on or off
transitions.edgeMedia: the clip's spare source frames beyond its trim when present, else its edge frame held for at most d/2
transitions.fit: each clip gives d/2 at a cut; a clip with transitions at both ends gives half of each; the maximum d is twice the smaller room, rounded down to 0.1 s

photosensitivity.note: Dip to white is one swell; Glitch cut at most 3 bursts a second

transitions.usage: One transition per cut, stored on the clip before the cut. A tile tap applies it and plays the cut once. Edits that make it not fit shorten it in the same undo step, down to 0.1 s, then remove it with a toast.

speed.note: User content, not chrome: clip speed and speed curves for video clips (P4-09). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a SpeedCatalog) next to OverlayCatalog. Preset ids are saved forever. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-09-speed.md.
speed.detachAudioOnlyWhen: constant speed 0.5 to 2 with sound kept; the new audio clip takes the speed
speed.keyframes: keep their share of the clip's length

curve.xAxis: position in the clip's own picture (source), 0 to 1
curve.interpolation: cosine ease between points in log speed
curve.audioJoin: short level dip at each join (Media3 cannot crossfade between speed pieces); a continuous time stretch is the fallback if the ear test fails

graph.note: content constants of the graph drawing, not chrome tokens

speed.usage: Constant 0.1x to 10x with tiles and a log slider; sound follows the speed with the pitch kept (as the sound clips' Speed in P3-09) or is muted by the user's choice. Length = trimmed source / speed; main clips ripple, overlays move lane.

freezeReverse.note: User content, not chrome: reverse and freeze frame (P4-10). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a FreezeReverseCatalog) next to OverlayCatalog. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-10-reverse-and-freeze.md.

reverse.copy: an all-intra reversed copy of the trimmed range in the app cache, never in the project

freezeReverse.usage: Reverse is a per-clip switch; Freeze frame splits the clip at the playhead and inserts a 2 s still of that frame as a photo-like main clip.

textAnimation.note: User content, not chrome: how a caption's in, out and loop animations and its ten looks draw, alike in preview and export (P4-11). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a TextAnimationCatalog) next to CaptionCatalog. Ids are saved forever. Changing a rule after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-11-text-animations-and-looks.md.

windows.inPlusOutAtMost: the item's length (the larger is cut first at draw time; stored values stay)

textAnimation.reveal: Typewriter and Erase clip the finished layout at a grapheme-cluster boundary; the text is never laid out again

photosensitivity.note: Only Blink changes brightness periodically; WCAG 2.3.1

textAnimation.looksNote: A duration of 0 means 'set when applied by the typewriter rule (40 ms a character, 0.5 s to 2 s)'. A look replaces font, color, outline, shadow, box and the three animations; the words, transform, timing and keyframes stay. The last style used also carries the animations.
textAnimation.usage: One In, one Out and one Loop per caption. Animations change only how the finished block is drawn (a transform about its center, an alpha, a reveal); the layout never changes. Time is the item's own time at the frame's presentation time; the only randomness (Shake) hashes the time rounded to 1/30 s and the item id.

stickerAnimation.note: User content, not chrome: stickers in video, animated GIF and WebP, the user's own files and the photo editor's GIF export (P4-12). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a StickerAnimationCatalog) next to PhotoCatalog. The sticker size rule is photo.sticker (35% of the shorter side at scale 1, 10% to 500%). Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-12-stickers-in-video.md.

landing.usage: At the playhead; an animated sticker lasts a whole number of its loops nearest 3 s (at least one, at most 10 s); with under 1 s of video left it ends at the end. Centered at scale 1 in the first free slot (video only; the photo editor lands every sticker in the center).

loop.frameAtTime: (t - item start + trimIn) mod loop length; a pure function of timeline time

gifExport.firstFrameTolerance: mean error under 6/255 against the PNG export (to be tightened at the first passing build)

stickerAnimation.usage: Stickers are items on the Stickers lane with their own copy of the file; animated ones always loop while the item lasts. WhatsApp packs list static stickers only.

cutoutVideo.note: User content, not chrome: background removal for people in video (P4-13). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a CutOutVideoCatalog) next to OverlayCatalog. Fixed rules: changing one after the closed test (about 25 Jan 2027) needs a schema bump. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-13-video-background-removal.md.
cutoutVideo.model: person segmentation (MediaPipe Image Segmenter, video mode); confirmed at the start of P4-13

cache.where: app cache, in source time, never in the project

cutoutVideo.pipeline: turn, mirror, crop, key and cut-out (alphas multiply), color edits, Fit or Fill, mask, framing, opacity, blend
cutoutVideo.usage: People only in v1 (owner, 8 Oct 2026). The cut is made once per source frame at no more than 30 frames a second and kept in the cache; the project keeps only softness, edge size, steadiness and strokes. Preview reads the cut at the model's size; export refines it at the output size.

templates.note: Content rules for the Templates tab and the Template screen (P4-05). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a TemplateCatalog). Template names, categories, slot labels and sample captions are catalog content in five languages, not app strings. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-05-templates.md.
templates.usage: A card opens the Template screen (preview, facts, slots, Open in editor). Opening builds an ordinary Project from the template's preset, so everything is editable. A template needs a poster still and a short muted preview video.

memeShortcuts.note: Content rules for the meme shortcuts (P4-14). Never read through MemixTheme; kept in one commonMain place (a MemeShortcutCatalog) next to EffectCatalog. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P4-14-meme-shortcuts.md.

quickCaption.span: the main clip under the playhead
quickCaption.style: the last style used, else the default

memeShortcuts.usage: Sound + zoom is a switch in the Meme sounds sheet's title row; Top & bottom is two typing steps over P1-10's entry bar; beat markers are tapped in or placed at the playhead and are snap and jump targets only.

watermark.note: User content, not chrome: the 'Memix' mark drawn into every free export (P1-13; owner, 8 Oct 2026: small text, top-left, 3% margin). Never read through MemixTheme, and never drawn in the editor preview; kept in one commonMain place next to the caption and canvas constants and drawn by the one text renderer as the top-most export overlay. Not saved in drafts, so changing a value needs no schema bump and affects only new exports. Spec: docs/ux/specs/P1-13-watermark.md.
watermark.usage: Font size 4% of the output's shorter side (43 px at 1080p); the glyphs' ink box starts 3% of the shorter side from the left and top edges (32 px at 1080p; two constants, so the owner's phase-end TikTok and Reels test can move only the top, about 0.13 for option B); white at 80% with a soft, unoffset black shadow at 50% (blur 15% of the font size) so it reads on bright footage without an outline. Above every layer, for the whole video. Not translated, not uppercased. Brand names have no WCAG contrast requirement (SC 1.4.3 logotype exception).
